entries.statement: A3's description does not state the communication mechanism between web/mobile client applications and their BFFs. The architecture diagram labels these edges 'HTTP/REST' as a conventional choice for client-to-BFF calls; no input confirms this protocol.
entries.resolution_needed: Confirm the client-to-BFF transport (HTTP/REST, or another protocol) if it must be documented precisely.

entries.statement: A3's description lists 'administrator status refresh' among the events published through the outbox but does not state which core module (Fleet & Availability or Rentals) emits it. The diagram attributes it to the Fleet & Availability module as the most direct owner of fleet status, which is an inference beyond what the alternative states.
source_refs: Timely bike availability and location tracking
entries.resolution_needed: Confirm which module is responsible for publishing the administrator status-refresh event.

entries.statement: Delivery of the physical unlock signal (Rentals module to the bike lock/telematics interface) is drawn as a direct edge in the diagram for clarity, but the alternative only assumes an adapter-wrapped interface exists (S2-G4) without describing which core module calls it or the protocol used.
entries.resolution_needed: Confirm which module calls the lock/telematics adapter and what interface it exposes.

entries.statement: All open assumptions and unresolved gaps carried into the ADR's 'Assumptions and Unresolved Gaps' section (S1-G1, S1-G16, S1-G18, S1-G43, S1-G44, S1-G50, S1-G52, S1-G4, S2-G2, S2-G4, S2-G10, S2-G11, S2-G12, S2-G16, S2-G17, S3-G1 through S3-G11) remain as recorded in their originating stage registers; this stage register does not duplicate them, only references them from the ADR.
